To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the class of parallel functions is closed under composition; 2) the class of sequential functions is closed under recursion; 3) every function can be decomposed into parallel and sequential ones; and 4) the class of all functions is closed under both composition and recursion.
the parallel functions are more powerful than the sequential ones with respect to the composition and recursion.
the sequential and parallel functions are incomparable with respect to composition but sequential ones are more powerful than parallel ones with respect to recursion.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the problem of the comparative strength of different classes of sequential and parallel functions, and the results obtained are of importance in the theory of computability and the theory of computation.
the problem of the representation of sequential and parallel functions by means of sequential and parallel operations.
the question: “How can the class of sequential functions be extended to the class of parallel functions?”
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sequential functions form a proper class of parallel ones.
the class of all sequential functions (including all partial recursive functions) is the most powerful class of functions with respect to both composition and recursion.
the class of parallel functions is the most powerful class and, in fact, it contains all other classes as subclasses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in general, parallel functions are more powerful than sequential ones.

sequential functions have the greatest power, parallel functions have the next greatest, and sequential functions with the greatest number of arguments have the least power among all the classes of functions considered here.
the class of sequential functions is closed under composition and recursion while the class of parallel functions is not.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sequential and parallel functions are incomparable in power with respect to composition and recursion.
the sequentiality of functions can be used to prove that they are not recursive in the sense of D.Scott.
the sequential functions are the most powerful ones.
